title: chat-core: Provider trait + inventory registry
description:
Define crates/chat-core/src/provider.rs as the sole abstraction over all backends.

Background: The plan's open-closed requirement says chat-core must never import a concrete provider. Adding Gemini later must be cargo new crates/provider-gemini with no core edit.

Scope:
- Structs: ProviderHandle { conversation_id, parent_message_id }, ChatReq { prompt, system, attachments_text }, ChatResp { content, conversation_id, message_id }, Session { valid, expiry }.
- Trait: Provider { id() -> &'static str, context_limit() -> usize, auth(&str) -> Session, chat(&ProviderHandle, ChatReq) -> ChatResp, prepare_attachments(&[PathBuf]) with default impl calling attach::default_prepare_attachments }.
- Registry: ProviderEntry { id, factory: fn() -> Box<dyn Provider> } with inventory::collect! and helpers get_provider(id) + list_providers().
- Add unit test: mock provider registers via inventory::submit! in test, get_provider returns it.

Why before everything: every other bead depends on this contract. No provider can be implemented until the trait is frozen.

Files: crates/chat-core/src/provider.rs, crates/chat-core/src/lib.rs
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p chat-core mock provider via inventory; get_provider returns it; no provider imported in core

title: chat-core: config.rs — config.toml as source of truth
description:
Implement crates/chat-core/src/config.rs: ~/.config/chat-cli/config.toml is the source of truth.

Background: default_provider must be an explicit field, not inferred from login order. First login sets it if absent; later logins must not overwrite. --config <path> overrides the default path for tests/CI.

Scope:
- Structs: Config { default_provider: Option<String>, providers: HashMap<String, ProviderConfig> }, ProviderConfig { session_token, access_token, access_token_expiry: Option<String> } — all Serialize/Deserialize.
- Methods: Config::config_path(override) -> PathBuf, load(override) -> Self (Ok(default) if missing), save(override) (create_dir_all, toml::to_string_pretty, write to .tmp then rename, chmod 0600 on unix), ensure_default_provider(id) (sets only if None).
- Unit tests: load missing file, save+reload round-trip, ensure_default_provider first vs second login, 0600 permissions, --config override path.

Considerations: atomic write+rename prevents truncation on crash; 0600 is required because session tokens are secrets.

Files: crates/chat-core/src/config.rs
acceptance_criteria: load missing file gives default; save+reload round-trip; ensure_default_provider first vs second login; chmod 0600; config override path

title: chat-core: attach.rs — -a resolution and injection
description:
Implement crates/chat-core/src/attach.rs: resolve all -a forms into Vec<PathBuf> and inject into prompt.

Background: The CLI supports four -a forms plus implicit stdin. Providers may later override prepare_attachments for real upload (ChatGPT /backend-api/files) without touching core — core's default is text injection.

Scope:
- resolve_attachments(&[String]) -> Vec<PathBuf>: for each entry, comma-split, handle @file indirection (read list file, skip empty and # comments), glob expansion via glob crate (bail if matched none), dedup preserving order with HashSet.
- default_prepare_attachments(&[PathBuf]) -> String: guards 1MB/file and 5MB total, read_to_string as UTF-8 (bail on non-UTF8), inject <<<FILE: path>>>\n```\ncontent\n```\n\n.
- maybe_read_stdin_as_attachment(has_attachments: bool) -> String: if has_attachments is false and stdin is piped (not tty via IsTerminal), read stdin to string, treat as one virtual file with same size guard.
- Unit tests: comma split, @file, glob match and no-match, dedup, size guards, UTF-8 error, stdin mock.

Files: crates/chat-core/src/attach.rs
acceptance_criteria: comma At-file glob dedup; 1MB per file and 5MB total guards; UTF-8 bail; stdin piped case — all tested

title: chat-core: budget.rs — fail-fast with breakdown

- Function budget_check(system: Option<&str>, history_text, attachments_text, prompt, limit) -> Result<(), BudgetError>: total = sum of lens, bail if total > limit. POC uses byte/char count (no tokenizer).
- Unit tests: under limit passes, over limit fails with correct breakdown, system None treated as 0.

title: provider-chatgpt: pow.rs — Keccak-f[1600] rounds 1..23
description:
Implement crates/provider-chatgpt/src/pow.rs: sentinel PoW solver.

Background: ChatGPT sentinel uses Keccak-f[1600] rounds 1..23 (skip round 0), same variant as DeepSeek DeepSeekHashV1. This is the highest-risk bead — a single bit error breaks auth. Port faithfully and bring test vectors.

Scope:
- Keccak-f[1600] with rounds 1..23 only, rate=136, padding 0x06+0x80.
- solve_pow(challenge_hex: &str, salt: &str, expire_at: i64, difficulty: i64) -> Result<i64>: pre-absorb prefix = format!("{}_{}_", salt, expire_at) into Keccak state, zero-alloc nonce suffix per iteration, check ctx cancellation every 1024 nonces if async, compare 32-byte hash to challenge.
- Bring test vectors from the reference PoW implementation (known challenge/salt/expire/difficulty -> expected nonce). Add #[test] for at least two vectors.
- Consider sharing this crate with provider-deepseek if sentinels converge — keep the solver in provider-chatgpt for POC, extract to a shared crate later if needed.

Files: crates/provider-chatgpt/src/pow.rs
acceptance_criteria: two test vectors pass Keccak rounds 1..23; rate 136 and prefix pre-absorb verified

title: provider-chatgpt: auth — rolling refresh
description:
Implement auth for crates/provider-chatgpt/src/lib.rs: rolling session refresh.

Background: Token is pasted once (manual cookie copy of __Secure-next-auth.session-token). Every chat must do the same rolling refresh the browser does, otherwise the session silently dies.

Scope:
- auth(token: &str) -> Session: GET /api/auth/session with Cookie: __Secure-next-auth.session-token=<token>, parse { accessToken, expires }, return Session { valid, expiry }.
- Before each chat: if access_token is expired/missing, call auth to refresh and persist the new Set-Cookie value and access_token back to config.toml (atomic write).
- Store access_token + expiry in [providers.chatgpt] alongside session_token.
- Unit test with mocked HTTP for success, 401, and refresh path.

title: provider-chatgpt: chat — sentinel + conversation
description:
Implement chat for crates/provider-chatgpt/src/lib.rs: send a message via web endpoints.

Background: This is the core user-facing path for chat-cli -p ... --provider chatgpt with -a and --new/--continue.

Scope:
- chat(&ProviderHandle, ChatReq) -> ChatResp:
  1) Ensure access_token is fresh (call auth refresh if needed).
  2) If sentinel challenged: POST /sentinel/chat-requirements/prepare|finalize and solve PoW via pow.rs, attach proof header/token.
  3) Build conversation payload: if handle.conversation_id is None -> new conversation (fresh parent_message_id uuid); else continue with stored ids. Attachments already in req.attachments_text.
  4) POST /backend-api/conversation (SSE or JSON), parse streamed response, return ChatResp { content, conversation_id, message_id } (both uuids).
- Cross-cutting: verbose logging to stderr when --verbose, proper error mapping (401 -> re-login hint, 429 -> suggest --provider deepseek).
- Integration test with mocked HTTP (mockito) covering new and continue paths.

Files: crates/provider-chatgpt/src/lib.rs
acceptance_criteria: mocked POST backend-api conversation new and continue return ChatResp; 401 maps to relogin hint
close_reason: Implemented in 5bc4e49: sentinel requirements + conversation POST with SSE parsing, 401/429 mapping; 35/35 provider tests, workspace clippy clean

title: chat-cli: dispatch.rs — provider resolve to chat pipeline
description:
Implement crates/chat-cli/src/dispatch.rs: the wiring layer that connects all core pieces.

Background: This is where provider resolution, attach, budget, history, and provider chat are sequenced. It must be correct about --new/--continue semantics and fail-fast on cross-provider misuse.

Scope:
- run(Args): if subcommand present -> run_subcommand, else require prompt and call run_chat.
- run_subcommand: auth login (hidden input via rpassword if --token missing, call Provider::auth to validate, save to config with ensure_default_provider, first-login-only default), status (list providers from config), logout, history list/show/rm, config set/get.
- run_chat: 1) resolve provider: --provider flag -> config.default_provider -> bail with clear message; 2) get_provider from inventory; 3) resolve_attachments + provider.prepare_attachments + maybe_read_stdin_as_attachment; 4) resolve_history into (ProviderHandle, history_text) honoring --new/--continue[<id>]/default-most-recent with cross-provider guard; 5) budget_check with per-segment breakdown; 6) build ChatReq and call provider.chat; 7) persist_history (update provider ids, append user+assistant turns); 8) println content to stdout.
- Tests: mock provider via inventory, cover auth/config/history and chat with --new/--continue, cross-provider error, stdin case.

Files: crates/chat-cli/src/dispatch.rs, main.rs
acceptance_criteria: mock provider via inventory: auth config history and chat with new/continue plus cross-provider error and stdin
